key_findings: **20 named ActorBase-derived classes confirmed** (all in Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control namespace):
- 10 single-vftable classes: WidgetBase, DebugBase, DirectorBase, Debug, AreaBase, SpreadSheet, CharaBase, WorldMaster, CommandDebuggerBase, plus 1 more (counted in single-vftable below).
- 8 multi-inheritance classes (2 vftables at +0x00 + +0x60): JudgeBase, GroupBase, ItemBase, QuestBase, Table, WidgetHandle, CommandBase, String, Math (9 actually). Same MI pattern as StatusBase.

- 2 triple-vftable classes (Global + CutScene): write 3 vftables including a Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaThreadEndListenerInterface secondary at +0x68. These classes implement BOTH ActorBase-chain AND LuaThreadEndListenerInterface - first cross-cutting interface evidence in the Lua-bridge.

- FUN_0075F9B0 (7481 bytes) = Lua-control AGGREGATE FACTORY. Calls 14+ different ctors. Likely the LuaControl REGISTRY initializer that creates one instance of each control class at startup. 1 caller (FUN_007634B0).

- FUN_007185E0 (94 bytes) = ActorBase-allocator-helper. Allocates 0x60 bytes + calls ActorBase::ctor but doesn't write a derived class vftable in the visible body. Possibly a bare-ActorBase factory or has inlined derived ctor calls.

**Cross-cutting interface revelation**: 2 of the 20 named classes (Global + CutScene) participate in Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaThreadEndListenerInterface via multi-inheritance with 3 vftables. Suggests there's a separate Lua-bridge interface for thread-end listening alongside the LuaControl hierarchy. Later work could enumerate other LuaThreadEndListenerInterface implementors.
